claims.text: Powder-based extrusion of Group IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys requires a two-stage thermal history.
Low-temperature vacuum annealing decomposes the hydride precursors and removes hydrogen.
Low-temperature vacuum annealing can remove hydrogen without triggering oxygen uptake.
High-pressure extrusion below the alpha-HCP precipitation threshold can densify the alloy while suppressing brittle-phase formation.
The required vacuum pressure is below 10^-6 Pa.
The required initial annealing temperature is 300–500 °C.
An extrusion temperature of 1000–1200 °C is below the alpha-HCP onset for the target alloys.
Avoiding the alpha-HCP nucleation window retains a metastable BCC solid solution.
Rapid hydrogen removal and oxygen exclusion facilitate retention of the metastable BCC phase.
Hydride decomposition releases hydrogen gas.
Performing hydride decomposition in vacuum prevents hydrogen-induced cracking.
Excluding oxygen prevents the formation of brittle oxide inclusions.
Brittle oxide inclusions act as nucleation sites for alpha-HCP precipitation.
High-pressure extrusion forces densification of the powder.
Maintaining the specified thermal window preserves a ductile BCC phase and thereby maximizes high-temperature yield strength.
The proposed process will produce a dense bulk alloy with a homogeneous BCC microstructure and no catastrophic cracking.
The proposed process will reduce alloy oxygen content to below 100 ppm.
Suppressing alpha-HCP precipitation will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
Standard powder-metallurgy processing in inert gas or air typically causes oxygen uptake, alpha-HCP precipitation, and brittle fracture during densification.
The process succeeds only when extrusion remains below the alpha-HCP nucleation threshold and residual oxygen from gases or container walls is sufficiently excluded.

contradictions.description: The conditions designate 1000–1200 °C as below the alpha-HCP onset, while the uncertainty field states that the exact critical alpha-HCP precipitation temperature is not known for the specific alloys.
The conditions prescribe a vacuum pressure below 10^-6 Pa, while the uncertainty field states that the pressure needed to prevent oxygen uptake in this hydride-decomposition context is unknown.
